fact: Tom Allen and Bill Ryall gave sparring exhibitions throughout the country after arriving in America.
Joe Coburn sparred with Tom Allen at the Bowery Theater, New York, when Allen first came to America.
In 1868, before Joe Coburn's match with Jem Mace, Joe Goss, Tom Allen and Bill Rayne were pitted against Coburn as a test, and Coburn beat them all.
Tom Allen boxed at Mozart Hall, Broadway and Biddle Street, St. Louis, in the period from about 1868 to 1874.
Tom Allen and Bill Ryall were to give a sparring set-to at Prof. Henry's hall in St. Louis on Saturday night for the benefit of the poor.
Tom Allen sparred Mike McCoole in the windup of a Saturday night exhibition, and McCoole bled from a reopened cut on his forehead.
Tom Allen proposed to give an exhibition a few days before his departure to meet McCoole.
Tom Allen gave a sparring exhibition in Cincinnati on 5 June 1869, with a well-attended benefit at the National Theatre that evening.
Tom Allen left St. Louis on 29 June 1869 for an extensive sparring tour.
Tom Allen was to give a sparring exhibition with Jim Coyne at Vincennes, Indiana, on the night of 30 June 1869.
Tom Allen and Jim Coyne were to give a gloves exhibition at Cincinnati on Thursday night, 1 July 1869.
Tom Allen gave a sparring exhibition at Benson's Theatre in Louisville on 5 July 1869, where the hall was crowded, and had a set-to with his trainer Jim Coyne.
Tickets for a steamboat excursion to the battleground on 17 August 1869 were sold for the benefit of Tom Allen or Charley Gallagher, the steamer leaving the foot of Elm Street that morning.
A benefit for Tom Allen was said to be planned at Frank's Hall on Friday night, 27 August 1869.
Tom Allen gave a sparring exhibition at the Opera House in Leavenworth, Kansas, on 28 August 1869, to a large crowd.
Tom Allen sparred with Harry Slater at Brady's Hall in St. Joseph, Missouri, on 31 August 1869.
Friends held a sparring reception for Tom Allen at the Hotel du Nord in the Bowery, New York, in September 1869, where Allen sparred with Dwyer of Brooklyn.
Tom Allen and Jim Coyne gave a sparring exhibition in Rochester, New York, on the night of 18 September 1869.
Tom Allen was to give an exhibition in Cincinnati on Saturday, 16 October 1869, probably at Mozart Hall.
Tom Allen was to have had a benefit at Mozart Hall, Cincinnati, on 30 October 1869.
In 1870 Tom Allen worked and sparred on exhibition with Jem Mace in New York, and afterwards toured the country with him, making good money for both.
Tom Allen sparred Joe Coburn at Mozart Hall on 25 April 1870, the wind-up of a sparring exhibition, with Coburn the more active and landing about twice as many blows.

A testimonial benefit for Tom Allen, with a $1,000 championship belt to be presented to him, was set for 30 April 1870 at the Theatre Comique (old Mozart Hall), corner of Fifth and Biddle; it was postponed to 4 May 1870 after the Biddle Street sewer caved in, and then postponed a second time.
A sparring match between Jem Mace and Tom Allen was planned for Saturday night, 28 May 1870, with the place still to be chosen.

Tom Allen and Jem Mace sparred three rounds in a friendly exhibition at Brady's Curriculum in Jersey City on 10 June 1870, where Mr. Abrahams displayed the belt each had been presented with by friends.
Jem Mace and Tom Allen fought four rounds with gloves in a sparring match at Tammany Hall, New York, on 17 June 1870, and Allen's champion's belt was exhibited there.
In an exhibition for the Chicago fire sufferers in St. Louis, Tom Allen stopped Ned O'Baldwin in a glove bout, showing clear superiority.
A sparring exhibition between Tom Allen and Jem Mace, with Cusick and Hollywood, was planned for 2 June 1871 at Carroll's Varieties in Kansas City.
Billy Madden and George Siler toured the United States in 1872 with Tom Allen, Joe Goss and Joe Coburn.

Tom Allen had a complimentary benefit as Champion of the World at the Theatre Comique on 25 and 26 September 1873, sparring Jack Madden, with Arthur Chambers and Patsy Sheppard also boxing; the house was crowded.
Tom Allen was on exhibition as an attraction at a booth during the St. Louis Fair in October 1873.
Tom Allen had a benefit at Deagle's Theatre in St. Louis on the night of 28 October 1873, with sparring planned, including Ben Hogan, Arthur Chambers and Young Ryan.
Tom Allen was to give an exhibition in Kansas City in November 1873 with Arthur Chambers and Jack Madden.
Tom Allen said Arthur Chambers and Billy Edwards were to come to St. Louis about 7 March 1874 to give sparring exhibitions at Deagle's for a week, to test the bill.
Tom Allen sparred Joe Coburn at a benefit for Mike Coburn at Harry Hill's in New York in 1875, on condition that Coburn promise not to throw him, and Coburn gave that promise.
A sparring exhibition between Tom Allen and Jimmy Walsh of London, advertised for Rickard's benefit, was stopped by the authorities under a statute prohibiting public sparring exhibitions.
A benefit for Tom Allen was held at Harry Hill's in New York in March 1875, with Allen in the main bout against Jim Coyne.
Tom Allen went on an eastern sparring tour in March 1875, giving exhibitions in New York, Boston, Philadelphia and Pittsburg.
At his benefit at the Grand Central Variety Theater in Philadelphia in March 1875, Tom Allen was presented with a large solid silver goblet.
Ed O'Baldwin, the Irish giant, asked Tom Allen to travel with him giving sparring exhibitions across the country in July 1875, and Allen declined.

Tom Allen left St. Louis on 1 December 1875 to give sparring exhibitions in Louisville, Cincinnati, Columbus, Cleveland, Pittsburg, Buffalo and other cities, with Young Donnelly to travel with him as sparring partner.

After the Goss fight in 1876, Tom Allen and Jem Mace travelled together around the country, Allen billed as champion of the world, and Billy Harrison went ahead as their advance agent to prepare exhibitions in California.

Tom Allen and his trainer Ned Donnelly put on the gloves and sparred at an entertainment, a private benefit for Donnelly given by members of Tom Allen's Gymnasium Club in St. Louis, on 22 February 1876.

Tom Allen played a one-week engagement at the Theatre Comique, Pine Street, St. Louis, in March 1876, setting to with the gloves with Ned Donnelly every evening in the crib scene from Tom and Jerry; it was the last three nights of the run.
Tom Allen gave a sparring exhibition in Louisville on 11 March 1876, assisted by his trainers Ned Donnelly and Jack Madden and local boxers.

A grand benefit for Tom Allen was held at the Theatre Comique, St. Louis, on Thursday 30 March 1876, with a glove set-to against Ned Donnelly, a wrestling match and a variety bill, and the recovered belt presented to him.
Tom Allen gave sparring exhibitions at the Comique in St. Louis some weeks before May 1876.
Immediately after signing the articles, Tom Allen left Cincinnati in May 1876 to give exhibitions in several of the most prominent Eastern cities.
Tom Allen sparred Tom Kelly in the crib scene from Tom and Jerry at Kelly's benefit at the Theatre Comique in St. Louis on 5 May 1876, Allen being described as the champion.
Tom Allen's friends gave him a complimentary benefit at the Avenue Theatre in Washington on 10 June 1876, where he appeared in a boxing exhibition with his trainer Jack Madden.
Tom Allen and his trainer Jack Madden gave nightly glove set-tos at the Comique in St. Louis, with the last appearance on 28 June 1876.

Tom Allen and Tom Kelly appeared on stage at the Theatre Comique in St. Louis on 21 September 1876, in Allen's farewell benefit, with a bout between Allen and Kelly; they were given a grand reception before a crowded house.
Tom Allen and Jem Mace gave a boxing match at the Theatre Comique in St. Louis on 24 and 25 October 1876.
In 1877 Tom Allen and George Rooke gave sparring exhibitions throughout England.
Tom Allen's first exhibition in Birmingham, his home town, in 1877 drew the largest crowd for such an affair in many years.
At Manchester in 1877, Tom Allen knocked George Rooke out of time with a left during a sparring bout with gloves.
Tom Allen was reported to be matched against Tomkins Gilbert, champion sparrer of England, in a sparring match for 50 pounds a side.

Tom Allen made a complimentary exhibition appearance in the art gallery of Madison Square Garden, New York, on 27 November 1882, his first public appearance in America since returning from England; he and George Rooke rounded up the exhibition, and Allen fell heavily at the end of the last round.
Tom Allen had a set-to with George Rooke in December 1882, agreed to be without rough work, and said he fell in it only because his foot broke through the staging.

Tom Allen sparred three rounds of light tapping with Morris O'Connell as the windup of O'Connell's farewell benefit at Tom Kelly's in St. Louis on 21 February 1883, his first appearance with the gloves since returning to St. Louis.
Tom Allen was announced to appear at a grand athletic tournament at the old Turner Hall in Belleville in March 1883.

Tom Allen was advertised, as the retired champion of the world, for a sparring exhibition at Flannigan's Hall, East St. Louis, on 29 March 1883, which was not held; Allen told Chief Kerrigan he did not wish to break the law.

Tom Allen and Tom Kelly, the ex-champions, sparred the wind-up at the Fourth of July athletic tournament at the Union Base Ball Grounds, St. Louis, on 4 July 1884, for the Union Club cup; it was four friendly rounds and was Allen's last boxing appearance.
Tom Allen was to spar four rounds with Hugh McManus as the wind-up of a benefit for Pittsburg pugilist Jack King at the Kelly Athletic Club on 23 February 1888.
Tom Allen's place at 619 Market Street advertised a free concert and boxing by the city's best boxers every evening, in May and June 1888.
Friends led by R. W. L. Gillespie planned a benefit of boxing bouts and feats of strength, probably at the West End Club, to pay for a monument and the care of Allen's grave.
